chapters.title: A man washing together with his wife
Washing with a sa‘ or thereabouts
Pouring over the head three times
Beginning with the hilab or scent when washing
Rinsing the mouth and drawing water into the nose for janabah
Wiping the hand with earth so that it is cleaner
May someone in janabah put his hand into the vessel before washing it, if there is no dirt on his hand other than janabah?

arabic_blocks: [245] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال : أخبرنا مالك عن هشام عن أبيه عن عائشة زوج النبي ﷺ أن النبي ﷺ كان إذا اغتسل من الجنابة بدأ فغسل يديه ثم يتوضأ كما يتوضأ للصلاة ثم يدخل أصابعه في الماء فيخلل بها أصول شعره ثم يصب على رأسه ثلاث غرف بيديه ثم يفيض الماء على جلده كله
english_blocks: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Hisham, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

Whenever the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, bathed for janabah, he began by washing his hands. Then he would perform ablution as he performed ablution for prayer. Then he would put his fingers into the water and work them through the roots of his hair. Then he would pour three handfuls over his head with his two hands, then pour water over all his skin.
entries.english_status: Personal prototype: AI-assisted working translation; two Arabic printed witnesses and two English translation families compared. Independent Arabic, English and context review pending.

notes: The full chain, the identification of Aisha as the Prophet’s wife, and both honorifics remain explicit. The chain ends before the description of the Prophet’s washing.
The selected sequence remains hands, ablution, fingers through hair roots, three handfuls with both hands, then water over all the skin. No sequence is harmonized with a different narration.
Janabah is retained as a source term; no legal gloss or modern volume conversion is inserted into the narration.

arabic_blocks: [246] حدثنا محمد بن يوسف قال : حدثنا سفيان عن الأعمش عن سالم بن أبي الجعد عن كريب عن ابن عباس عن ميمونة زوج النبي ﷺ قالت توضأ رسول الله ﷺ وضوءه للصلاة غير رجليه وغسل فرجه وما أصابه من الأذى ثم أفاض عليه الماء ثم نحى رجليه فغسلهما هذه غسله من الجنابة
english_blocks: Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from al-A‘mash, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja‘d, from Kurayb, from Ibn ‘Abbas, from Maymunah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, performed his ablution for prayer except for his feet, and washed his private parts and whatever had been soiled. Then he poured water over himself, then moved his feet aside and washed them. This was his washing for janabah.
entries.english_status: Personal prototype: AI-assisted working translation; two Arabic printed witnesses and two English translation families compared. Independent Arabic, English and context review pending.

notes: The full chain through Salim ibn Abi al-Jad, Kurayb and Ibn Abbas is retained, including Maymunah’s description as the Prophet’s wife.

The order of actions follows this selected text: ablution except feet, washing the private parts and soiling, water, then moving and washing the feet. The text is not reordered to reconcile it with other accounts.
The wording “whatever had been soiled” renders وما أصابه من الأذى without adding a specified bodily fluid or a legal ruling.

arabic_blocks: [247] حدثنا آدم بن أبي إياس قال : حدثنا ابن أبي ذئب عن الزهري عن عروة عن عائشة قالت كنت أغتسل أنا والنبي ﷺ من إناء واحد من قدح يقال له الفرق
english_blocks: Adam ibn Abi Iyas related to us. He said: Ibn Abi Dhi’b related to us, from al-Zuhri, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah, who said:
The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and I used to bathe from a single vessel, from a bowl called al-faraq.
entries.english_status: Personal prototype: AI-assisted working translation; two Arabic printed witnesses and two English translation families compared. Independent Arabic, English and context review pending.

notes: The selected digital reporting verb is حدثنا before Ibn Abi Dhib. The historical print has حدثني there; the modern print agrees with the selected plural form. The digital text is not silently harmonized with the historical variant.
Both the general vessel and the named bowl, al-faraq, remain in the English. No modern capacity is added.

arabic_blocks: [248] حدثنا عبد الله بن محمد قال : حدثني عبد الصمد قال : حدثني شعبة قال : حدثني أبو بكر ابن حفص قال : سمعت أبا سلمة يقول دخلت أنا وأخو عائشة على عائشة فسألها أخوها عن غسل النبي ﷺ فدعت بإناء نحوا من صاع فاغتسلت وأفاضت على رأسها وبيننا وبينها حجاب قال أبو عبد الله قال يزيد بن هارون وبهز والجدي عن شعبة قدر صاع
english_blocks: ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Samad related to me. He said: Shu‘bah related to me. He said: Abu Bakr ibn Hafs related to me. He said: I heard Abu Salamah saying:

‘A’ishah’s brother and I went in to ‘A’ishah. Her brother asked her about the washing of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. She called for a vessel containing about a sa‘, then bathed and poured water over her head, with a screen between us and her.
Abu ‘Abd Allah said: Yazid ibn Harun, Bahz and al-Juddi said, from Shu‘bah: “The amount of a sa‘.”
entries.english_status: Personal prototype: AI-assisted working translation; two Arabic printed witnesses and two English translation families compared. Independent Arabic, English and context review pending.

notes: All three singular reporting verbs and the listening clause remain distinct in the chain. The full Abu Abd Allah closing note includes all three named transmitters.
The selected “about a sa” in the body and “the amount of a sa” in the closing note remain separate. The curtain or screen is retained.
The checked Khan-family EPUB body 1.5.251 omits the closing transmission note. Bewley 248 includes an abbreviated rendering of its amount phrase; the complete names are translated from the Arabic.

arabic_blocks: [249] حدثنا عبد الله بن محمد قال : حدثنا يحيى بن آدم قال : حدثنا زهير عن أبي إسحاق قال : حدثنا أبو جعفر أنه كان عند جابر بن عبد الله هو وأبوه وعنده قوم فسألوه عن الغسل ، فقال يكفيك صاع ، فقال رجل ما يكفيني ، فقال جابر كان يكفي من هو أوفى منك شعرا وخير منك ثم أمنا في ثوب
english_blocks: ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: Yahya ibn Adam related to us. He said: Zuhayr related to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: Abu Ja‘far related to us:

He and his father were with Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, and some people were with him. They asked him about washing, and he said: “A sa‘ is enough for you.” A man said: “It is not enough for me.” Jabir said: “It was enough for someone who had more hair than you and was better than you.” Then he led us in prayer in a single garment.
entries.english_status: Personal prototype: AI-assisted working translation; two Arabic printed witnesses and two English translation families compared. Independent Arabic, English and context review pending.

notes: The selected wording introduces Abu Jafar in third person and ends “he led us”; the change of person remains in the working English.
The unnamed man stays unnamed. No identification of “someone who had more hair” is inserted into the source wording. “A single garment” is retained without adding an action of putting it on.

arabic_blocks: [250] حدثنا أبو نعيم قال : حدثنا ابن عيينة عن عمرو عن جابر بن زيد عن ابن عباس أن النبي ﷺ وميمونة كانا يغتسلان من إناء واحد ، وقال يزيد بن هارون وبهز والجدي عن شعبة قدر صاع
قال أبو عبد الله كان ابن عيينة يقول أخيرا عن ابن عباس عن ميمونة والصحيح ما روى أبو نعيم
english_blocks: Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Ibn ‘Uyaynah related to us, from ‘Amr, from Jabir ibn Zayd, from Ibn ‘Abbas:
The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and Maymunah used to bathe from one vessel.
And Yazid ibn Harun, Bahz and al-Juddi said, from Shu‘bah: “The amount of a sa‘.”
Abu ‘Abd Allah said: Ibn ‘Uyaynah would later say: “From Ibn ‘Abbas, from Maymunah.” And the correct version is what Abu Nu‘aym related.

arabic_blocks: [251] حدثنا أبو نعيم قال : حدثنا زهير عن أبي إسحاق قال : حدثني سليمان بن صرد قال : حدثني جبير بن مطعم قال : قال رسول الله ﷺ : أما أنا فأفيض على رأسي ثلاثا وأشار بيديه كلتيهما

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “As for me, I pour over my head three times.” And he gestured with both his hands.

arabic_blocks: [252] حدثنا محمد بن بشار قال : حدثنا غندر قال : حدثنا شعبة عن مخول بن راشد عن محمد بن علي عن جابر بن عبد الله قال : كان النبي ﷺ يفرغ على رأسه ثلاثا

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pour over his head three times.

arabic_blocks: [253] حدثنا أبو نعيم قال : حدثنا معمر بن يحيى بن سام حدثني أبو جعفر قال : قال لي جابر وأتاني بن عمك يعرض بالحسن بن محمد بن الحنفية قال كيف الغسل من الجنابة فقلت : كان النبي ﷺ يأخذ ثلاثة أكف ويفيضها على رأسه ثم يفيض على سائر جسده ، فقال لي الحسن إني رجل كثير الشعر فقلت : كان النبي ﷺ أكثر منك شعرا
english_blocks: Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Ma‘mar ibn Yahya ibn Sam related to us. Abu Ja‘far related to me. He said: Jabir said to me:

“And your cousin came to me”—referring to al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah. “He said: ‘How is washing for janabah performed?’ I said: ‘The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to take three handfuls and pour them over his head, then pour over the rest of his body.’ Al-Hasan said to me: ‘I am a man with a lot of hair.’ I said: ‘The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had more hair than you.’”

notes: The full chain includes Ma‘mar ibn Yahya ibn Sam and the singular Abu Ja‘far reporting verb. The selected initial conjunction and the explanatory identification of the cousin are retained.

The dialogue belongs to Jabir’s account. Three handfuls, the rest of the body, the statement about much hair and the reply are all retained. The cousin is not replaced with a new name outside the source identification.
Both English comparisons supply water in the three-handful clause; the selected Arabic does not explicitly name it there. No modern volume or further washing action is inserted.

arabic_blocks: [254] حدثنا موسى قال : حدثنا عبد الواحد عن الأعمش عن سالم بن أبي الجعد عن كريب عن ابن عباس قال : قالت ميمونة وضعت للنبي ﷺ ماء للغسل فغسل يديه مرتين أو ثلاثا ثم أفرغ على شماله فغسل مذاكيره ثم مسح يده بالأرض ثم مضمض واستنشق وغسل وجهه ويديه ثم أفاض على جسده ثم تحول من مكانه فغسل قدميه
english_blocks: Musa related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahid related to us, from al-A‘mash, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja‘d, from Kurayb, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: Maymunah said:

I set out water for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to bathe. He washed his hands twice or three times, then poured onto his left hand and washed his private parts. Then he wiped his hand on the ground, then rinsed his mouth and drew water into his nose, and washed his face and hands. Then he poured over his body, then moved from his place and washed his feet.

notes: The selected digital chain names Musa alone. Both inspected prints name Musa ibn Ismail. The longer name is documented here and is not inserted into the selected chain.
The uncertainty “twice or three times” and the sequence of all actions are preserved. The hand wiped on the ground remains singular; no towel is borrowed from 256.

The Arabic has الاستنشاق (drawing water into the nose) without a separate blowing-out verb. Both English comparisons add blowing out; that additional action is not inserted into this working rendering. Hands/arms wording remains provisional for independent review.

arabic_blocks: [255] حدثنا محمد بن المثنى قال : حدثنا أبو عاصم عن حنظلة عن القاسم عن عائشة قالت كان النبي ﷺ إذا اغتسل من الجنابة دعا بشيء نحو الحلاب فأخذ بكفه فبدأ بشق رأسه الأيمن ثم الأيسر ، فقال بهما على رأسه
english_blocks: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us. He said: Abu ‘Asim related to us, from Hanzalah, from al-Qasim, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, bathed for janabah, he asked for something like a hilab. He took some in his palm and began with the right side of his head, then the left, then poured over his head with both hands.

notes: The selected digital and modern Arabic end على رأسه. The historical print adds وسط (middle) there. The working English follows the selected wording and does not add “middle”.

The English comparisons disagree about hilab: Bewley gives a milk-pot, whereas EPUB 1.5.258 treats it as scent. The term hilab is retained without resolving that identification inside the hadith. The chapter heading separately retains its explicit “or scent”.

Ibn Hajar’s Fath al-Bari, book of Ghusl, discussion of this chapter at printed pages 440–442, examines the vessel/scent readings and parallel pouring expressions. This supports the provisional action wording “poured” rather than treating قال here as spoken words. The source is linked as commentary, not independent translation approval.

arabic_blocks: [256] حدثنا عمر بن حفص بن غياث قال : حدثنا أبي حدثنا الأعمش قال : حدثني سالم عن كريب عن ابن عباس قال : حدثتنا ميمونة قالت صببت للنبي ﷺ غسلا فأفرغ بيمينه على يساره فغسلهما ثم غسل فرجه ، ثم قال بيده الأرض فمسحها بالتراب ثم غسلها ثم تمضمض واستنشق ثم غسل وجهه وأفاض على رأسه ثم تنحى فغسل قدميه ثم أتي بمنديل فلم ينفض بها
english_blocks: ‘Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath related to us. He said: My father related to us. Al-A‘mash related to us. He said: Salim related to me, from Kurayb, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: Maymunah related to us. She said:

I poured out water for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to bathe. He poured with his right hand onto his left and washed them both, then washed his private parts. Then he struck the ground with his hand and wiped it with earth, then washed it. Then he rinsed his mouth and drew water into his nose, then washed his face and poured over his head. Then he moved aside and washed his feet. Then a cloth was brought to him, but he did not dry himself with it.

notes: All selected reporting verbs remain, including the singular Salim clause and Maymunah’s feminine “related to us”. The full name Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath remains in the chain.

The hand used on the earth is singular and is washed afterwards. The dual hands earlier in the report stay distinct. The selected account mentions the face and pouring on the head, without importing the arm/body clauses from another narration.

Ibn Hajar’s Fath al-Bari, book of Ghusl, discussion of this chapter at printed page 443, explains قال بيده الأرض as a physical action and the cloth ending as not wiping/drying. The lexical explanation is separate from the source; no legal ruling or additional narration is inserted.

The complete ending with the unused cloth is retained. The two English comparisons support that sense; their plural earth-wiping hands and added blowing-out wording are not substituted for the selected Arabic.

arabic_blocks: [257] حدثنا الحميدي قال : حدثنا سفيان قال : حدثنا الأعمش عن سالم بن أبي الجعد عن كريب عن ابن عباس عن ميمونة أن النبي ﷺ اغتسل من الجنابة فغسل فرجه بيده ثم دلك بها الحائط ثم غسلها ثم توضأ وضوءه للصلاة فلما فرغ من غسله غسل رجليه

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, bathed for janabah. He washed his private parts with his hand, then rubbed the wall with it, then washed it. Then he performed his ablution for prayer. When he had finished his washing, he washed his feet.

arabic_blocks: [258] حدثنا عبد الله بن مسلمة أخبرنا أفلح عن القاسم عن عائشة قالت كنت أغتسل أنا والنبي ﷺ من إناء واحد تختلف أيدينا فيه

When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, bathed for janabah, he washed his hand.

And from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, the same.
